meta.title: Mr. Barker Goes to Washington
meta.subtitle: A Satirical Congress Micro-Sim
meta.worldNote: Everyone in Maple Creek and Washington can be any animal—teachers, bakers, librarians, and lawmakers alike. The Capitol power brokers you collide with just happen to lean into classic literary fables, while every bill satirizes purely how Congress functions.

artDirection.description: Crisp flat-graphic editorial print aesthetic inspired by Aviary Attorney: warm parchment paper, thick charcoal ink outlines, flat block shading, subtle newspaper halftones, bold congressional crimson, navy, brass gold, and ink black.

meters.label: Constituents
meters.description: District 9 (Maple Creek) voter approval and Election Day turnout.

meters.label: Party Standing
meters.description: Caucus loyalty, committee clout, and institutional backing.

meters.label: War Chest
meters.description: Campaign cash for airwave ads and defending against primary attacks.

barker.name: Rep. Barnaby Barker
barker.visualBrief: Earnest golden-tan floppy-eared freshman puppy in a slightly oversized off-the-rack navy suit, polka-dot bow tie, perked hopeful ears (droop when stressed).

sheep.name: Martha Ewe
sheep.visualBrief: No-nonsense community organizer with curly cream wool, round brass spectacles, forest-green knit cardigan, holding a town-hall clipboard.

wolf.name: Whip Fenrir Fang
wolf.visualBrief: Razor-sharp slate-gray wolf in a crisp charcoal pinstripe suit, crimson power tie, brass monocle, gleaming whip-count clipboard.

snake.name: Vesper Viper, Esq.
snake.visualBrief: Sleek emerald viper in a tailored brocade waistcoat, gold pocket-watch chain, tinted pince-nez glasses, calm unblinking poise.

pig.name: Rep. Wilbur Troughman
pig.visualBrief: Portly pink-and-cream veteran lawmaker in a burgundy three-piece waistcoat, brass suspenders, handlebar tusks, waving a gold fountain pen.

bear.name: Chairwoman Beatrice Kodiak
bear.visualBrief: Imposing brown bear in a structured tweed blazer, tortoiseshell spectacles, pearl pin, resting one paw on a massive oak gavel.

bird.name: Mags Magpie
bird.visualBrief: Sharp black-and-white magpie in a belted trench coat, tilted fedora with a 'PRESS' card tucked in the band, vintage flash-bulb camera.

fox.name: Sterling Foxworth
fox.visualBrief: Impossibly polished russet fox with focus-grouped coiffed fur, tailored navy blazer over cream turtleneck, blinding campaign smile.

constituentPostcards.sender: Mrs. Lupine (Wolf), 3rd-Grade Teacher — Maple Creek Elementary
constituentPostcards.note: Good luck on your first week, Barnaby! My class drew you a card—please fix the broken streetlamps by the bus stop!

constituentPostcards.sender: Sal Viper (Snake), Owner — Main Street Sourdough Bakery
constituentPostcards.note: Sending fresh cinnamon rolls to your office! Our town footbridge needs repairs bad—don't let the toll ferry push us out.

constituentPostcards.sender: Penny Mallard (Duck), Head Librarian — Maple Creek Library
constituentPostcards.note: We have six buckets catching rain in the children's wing. Hoping the Library Roof Act is as clean as its title!

constituentPostcards.sender: Old Man Boarwell (Pig), Retired Postal Carrier
constituentPostcards.note: Walked Route 4 for forty years. Keep an eye on the fine print in today's Post Office bill, pup—my knees tell me trouble's coming.
Heard they stuffed storm loans for small shops into a 1,200-page monster bill. How is anyone supposed to vote on that?!

constituentPostcards.sender: Martha Ewe (Sheep) & The Maple Creek Town Hall
constituentPostcards.note: Today's the big day for your Flagship Bill! The whole town is glued to the radio waiting to see if a freshman can get it passed.

constituentPostcards.sender: Dr. Oona Owl (Owl), High School Civics Teacher
constituentPostcards.note: We tried diagramming H.R. 615 on the chalkboard and broke three pieces of chalk. Please read the staff memo before stamping!

constituentPostcards.sender: Coach Bruno Bear (Bear), Maple Creek Youth Softball
constituentPostcards.note: Who is this Sterling Foxworth guy?! His face is on four billboards by the diner and he just arrived in town yesterday!

constituentPostcards.sender: Sal Viper & Mrs. Lupine — Joint Neighborhood Note
constituentPostcards.note: That flood-damaged bridge on Highway 9 really needs work, Barnaby—just watch out for whatever they buried on Page 3.
Polls open at sunrise tomorrow! Whatever happens in tonight's midnight vote, Maple Creek is watching.

archetypes.title: The Grassroots Idealist
archetypes.tagline: "No backroom strings. Just read the bills and do the job."
archetypes.description: Beloved across Maple Creek, running on bake-sale money. Leadership already worries you actually read footnotes.

archetypes.title: The Pragmatic Climber
archetypes.tagline: "You can't fix the institution from the hallway outside."
archetypes.description: Polished, balanced, and eager to make friends on every committee. Everyone assumes they can win you over.

archetypes.title: The Deal-Making Booster
archetypes.tagline: "Bring federal projects home first; ask questions later."
archetypes.description: Flush War Chest and warm ties with Appropriations, though local watchdogs and reporters check every receipt.

deskProps.label: Kodiak Rules Commendation

deskProps.label: Miniature Golden Ribbon-Cutting Scissors

endings.title: SUBPOENAED BEFORE THE CONFETTI DROPS
endings.headline: BREAKING: ETHICS BOARD RAIDS BARKER VICTORY PARTY OVER 'MYSTERY ESPRESSO MACHINE'
endings.subhead: You played the backroom game hard and got sloppy on camera—even the lobbyists are shredding your business card.
endings.epilogue: Mags Magpie wins a national journalism award for printing your sticky-note trail. Whip Fang issues a three-word statement: 'Barely met him.'

endings.title: THE ACCIDENTAL SPEAKER
endings.headline: SHOCK ON CAPITOL HILL: FRESHMAN BARKER UNANIMOUSLY DRAFTED AS SPEAKER!
endings.subhead: By keeping every promise, decoding Page 3, and earning Kodiak's seal, you pulled off the rarest feat in Congress.
endings.epilogue: Pundits spend months wondering how a wide-eyed rookie from Maple Creek unified the chamber without selling out—mostly because you actually read the bills.

endings.title: THE GRASSROOTS LEGEND
endings.headline: MR. BARKER GOES BACK TO WASHINGTON! DISTRICT 9 DEFIES THE MACHINE!
endings.subhead: Tiny War Chest, zero lobbyist strings—you won on sheer hometown turnout and stubborn honesty.
endings.epilogue: Sal Viper sends three trays of celebratory cinnamon rolls to Capitol Hill. Whip Fang quietly moves your office closer to the radiator, terrified of your next town hall.

endings.title: MASTER OF THE MACHINE
endings.headline: VOTERS BAFFLED AS BARKER WINS LANDSLIDE ON 40,000 GLOSSY ATTACK ADS
endings.subhead: Maple Creek barely recognizes the idealistic pup they elected, but disciplined spin, donor cash, and party muscle carried you home.
endings.epilogue: Your desk is solid mahogany now. You still keep Mrs. Lupine's faded class card tucked in a drawer—right behind the velvet briefcase.

endings.title: THE UNPREDICTABLE MAVERICK
endings.headline: NOBODY KNOWS WHAT REP. BARKER STANDS FOR—AND DISTRICT 9 CAN'T LOOK AWAY!
endings.subhead: Half-reformer, half-horse-trader, full-time headline magnet. You survived by keeping every caucus guessing.
endings.epilogue: Columnists debate all winter whether you are a principled independent or a master tactician. Even your own staff isn't completely sure.

endings.title: ONE-TERM IDEALIST
endings.headline: TOO HONEST FOR THE HILL? BARKER LOSES SEAT AFTER REFUSING TO PLAY BALL
endings.subhead: Your record stayed spotless, your War Chest stayed empty, and the airwaves belonged to your opponent.
endings.epilogue: You head home to Maple Creek with your tail high, a standing ovation at the diner, and a hit civics podcast called 'Wait, Did You Read Page 1,204?'

endings.title: OUT-FOXED AT THE POLLS
endings.headline: PRIMARY UPSET! STERLING FOXWORTH SWEEPS DISTRICT 9 AS BARKER COALITION COLLAPSES
endings.subhead: Squeezed between frustrated voters and vengeful insiders, your coalition buckled before the ballots were counted.
endings.epilogue: Within 48 hours, Vesper Viper slips an embossed business card under your door: 'Need a consulting gig, kid? Former reps make wonderful lobbyists.'

civicReceipts.summary: Unpopular earmarks or policy changes are routinely stapled onto popular bills right before a vote, forcing lawmakers into a painful binary: swallow the rider or look like they voted against the headline.
Combining hundreds of unrelated measures into one giant must-pass bill squeezes out amendment debate and guarantees critics can attack any 'Aye' or 'Nay' vote.
Passing a signature bill often requires adding targeted funding or concessions for colleagues' priorities—trading legislative purity to build a working floor majority.
Procedural motions and ballot phrasing are sometimes written in nested negatives so that voting 'Aye' achieves the opposite of what the friendly title suggests.
Leadership enforces discipline using committee assignments, endorsements, and donor networks—and defying the whip can invite a well-funded primary challenger.
Complex legislative trade-offs rarely fit in a six-second hallway clip, rewarding lawmakers who frame their votes quickly before opponents define them first.
Legislatures run on institutional memory: casting tough votes for colleagues builds political capital that can later be spent to pull reluctant votes onto your own bill.
